1.reason: Flushing fat/oil-containing food packets with nitrogen (an inert gas) displaces oxygen and prevents oxidative rancidity; this is the standard packaging method shown.

2.reason: Copper develops a green coating (basic copper carbonate) on prolonged exposure to moist air — this is corrosion of copper.

4.reason: Aluminium deposits Zn, Cu and Fe metal from all three sulphate solutions, so Al displaces each of them — Al is more reactive than Zn, Cu and Fe.

5.reason: Fatty foods like cheese become unfit due to rancidity (oxidation of fats/oils giving bad smell and taste).

6.reason: Zn is more reactive than Fe, so it displaces iron from FeSO4; the freshly deposited iron forms a greyish-black coating on the zinc granules.

7.reason: Zinc displaces the less reactive metal from CuSO4 (blue decolourises) and FeSO4 (green decolourises); no reaction with aluminium or zinc sulphate. So C (copper sulphate) and D (ferrous sulphate).

8.reason: Zinc sulphate solution is colourless; among the four colours (Green, Yellow, Blue, Colourless), tube IV is colourless.

9.reason: Zinc displaces Fe (from iron sulphate, III) and Cu (from copper sulphate, IV) as it is more reactive; no reaction with aluminium or zinc sulphate. Colour change in III and IV.

10.reason: KI + Pb(NO3)2 give a bright yellow precipitate of lead iodide (PbI2) by double displacement — X is lead iodide, a precipitate.

11.reason: Chips packets are flushed with nitrogen gas (inert) to remove oxygen and prevent rancidity of the fried snack.

14.reason: Fe is less reactive than Zn, so iron cannot displace zinc from ZnSO4 — no reaction occurs.

27.reason: Rusting requires both the iron metal (A) and the presence of moisture and air/oxygen (B); both conditions are necessary.

28.reason: Opposite of combination is decomposition. Equation 1 (NH4Cl->NH3+HCl, thermal) and equation 2 (2H2O->2H2+O2, electrolysis) are decomposition; equation 3 (Fe+H2SO4->FeSO4+H2) is displacement. So A and B.

29.reason: All three observations are correct: zinc granules are irregular in shape, are silvery grey, and turn brownish-black as copper deposits on them. So A, B and C.

31.reason: BaCl2 + (NH4)2SO4 -> BaSO4(insoluble ppt) + NH4Cl; the insoluble BaSO4 makes it a precipitation reaction AND it is a double displacement reaction. So statements (ii) precipitation and (iv) double displacement -> option (ii) and (iv).

32.reason: Quicklime + water -> Ca(OH)2 is exothermic (i) and gives a basic solution with pH > 7 (iv). So A and D.

33.reason: The defining condition of a balanced chemical equation is that the number of atoms of each element is equal on both sides (statement 1). The sum of coefficients need not be equal, and 'atoms and ions are conserved' is not the standard single defining statement, so the best choice is Statement 1, which is option A.

34.reason: Na2SO4 + BaCl2 double displacement: ions are exchanged (2), a precipitate BaSO4 forms (3) which is an insoluble salt (4). So B, C and D.

35.reason: 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2: Fe is oxidized (i), water is reduced (ii) and therefore water acts as the oxidizing agent (iv). Statement (iii) is false. So (i),(ii) and (iv).

36.reason: All four are correct: electrolysis of water is decomposition; nitrogen flushing prevents rancidity; melting of ice is a physical change; corrosion requires both air and moisture. So All of these.

37.reason: 2Ag + Cu(NO3)2 -> 2AgNO3 + Cu is not correct: Ag is less reactive than Cu and cannot displace it. The other three displacements are valid.

38.reason: CaO(s) + H2O(l) -> Ca(OH)2(aq) is a combination reaction (1) and is exothermic (2). It is not endothermic and not an oxidation reaction. So A and B.

39.reason: Correct fact: hydrogen is highly combustible and oxygen is a supporter of combustion (statement 4). Statements 1, 2 and 3 are all incorrect. So A, B and C.

45.reason: Covering with plastic, oiling/greasing, galvanising and painting are all valid rust-prevention methods. Option C is the odd one out because it merely states a use of galvanised pipes rather than describing a deliberate rust-prevention action, so it is taken as the incorrect method.

46.reason: Fe + 2HCl -> FeCl2 + H2: hydrogen gas and iron(II) chloride are produced.

47.reason: Corrosion, rancidity (slow oxidation) and combination reactions can involve oxidation; a double displacement reaction is an ion-exchange with no change in oxidation state, so it is not an oxidation reaction.

48.reason: Double displacement is a non-redox reaction (no change in oxidation states); decomposition, combination and displacement reactions are commonly redox.

49.reason: C(s) + 2S(s) -> CS2(l) - 92 kJ: energy is absorbed (the '-92 kJ' on the product side / formation of CS2 is endothermic). The others release energy (exothermic).

50.reason: FeSO4.7H2O is a hydrated salt (green vitriol); on heating it loses its water of crystallisation. FeS, Fe2O3 and FeCO3 carry no water of crystallisation.

51.reason: 2 KClO3 (x) --(y)--> 2 KCl (x) + O2 (z): x denotes the physical state (s) of KClO3 and KCl, y is the reaction condition written over the arrow (heat), and z is the physical state (g) of O2.

52.reason: Balanced: 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2. Hydrogen atoms = 4x2 = 8 in reactants and 4x2 = 8 in products. So 8 and 8.

53.reason: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so Fe placed in ZnSO4 shows no reaction (no colour/deposit change), while Zn placed in FeSO4 displaces iron (the green solution turns colourless and an iron deposit forms). Student C records exactly this pattern, so the correct reporter is C = option B.

54.reason: Fe is less reactive than Al, so no reaction with Al2(SO4)3 (colourless solution unchanged). Fe is more reactive than Cu, so it displaces Cu from CuSO4: the blue colour fades and a reddish-brown copper deposit forms. Student D records both correctly -> option D.

55.reason: Slaking of lime (CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2) is exothermic (ii) and the resulting lime water is basic with pH > 7 (iii). So (ii) and (iii).

56.reason: Dissolution of NaOH and of anhydrous CuSO4 in water is exothermic (temperature rises in A and B -> statement i). Dissolution of NaCl is endothermic (temperature falls in C -> statement iv). So (i) and (iv).

57.reason: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces Cu from copper sulphate; the liberated copper deposits as a reddish-brown coating on the iron nail. So copper sulphate.

58.reason: In FeSO4 solution, metals more reactive than iron (zinc and aluminium) displace iron, giving a black/dark iron deposit; copper (less reactive) gives no deposit and iron itself gives none. So zinc and aluminium.

59.reason: Zn + 2HCl -> ZnCl2 + H2. The evolved hydrogen does not support combustion, so the burning match stick is extinguished, and the escaping H2 itself burns with a characteristic pop sound.

The whole set-up demonstrates a gas being evolved; there is no thermometer or any temperature measurement shown, so the observed characteristic is evolution of a gas (option C).

13.reason: The model shows an electron transferred from neutral atom A to neutral atom B, giving A+ (A loses an electron = oxidized) and B- (B gains an electron = reduced). Simultaneous oxidation and reduction by electron transfer is a redox reaction (option A).
